bullets.title: AI/momentum selloff accelerates: hedge funds reverse all 2025 net buying in 5 sessions
bullets.body: Goldman Sachs prime reports global AI stocks saw second-largest net selling in a year (-2.8 Z-score Oct 8-14), with hedge funds reversing all cumulative net buying since start of 2025. Net allocation to global AI stocks dropped from 31.7% peak to 26.1% (49th percentile). TMT L/S managers down -2.7%, now -4.5% MTD; overall net leverage at 73.3%, 6th percentile vs. past year. Prime HF intraday update shows Global Fundamental L/S down 0.9% (-1.2 SD) on the day, down every session this week for a -2.9% weekly drawdown, with momentum down 3.4 SD and crowded shorts squeezing +1.2 SD.

bullets.title: Hot CPI triggers 50% Oct hike odds; core PCE tracking 32-36bps — Fed likely skips Oct, hikes Dec
bullets.body: September core CPI came in at +0.335% m/m vs. +0.24% expected, sending Oct hike odds to ~45-50%. Core PCE is tracking 0.32-0.36% m/m for September; 3- and 6-month annualized core PCE pace rises to 2.77% and 2.86% respectively, with underlying inflation estimated near 3.25%. Multiple sources expect Fed to skip October but hike in December, with Williams, Warsh, Bowman signaling patience. Fed funds remain below nominal GDP growth (sub-4% vs. 6.3% nominal GDP), keeping policy still technically accommodative.

bullets.title: September macro data blowout: retail sales +0.8%, PPI +1.3% — but claims still near historic lows
bullets.body: September nominal retail sales beat consensus at +0.8% m/m, a record high; unadjusted retail sales rose 6.8% YoY (consumer electronics +8.8%, sporting goods +9.1%). Headline PPI surged +1.3% m/m vs. +0.6% expected; core PPI +0.7% vs. +0.3% consensus. Initial jobless claims fell to 199k, below 200k for fifth consecutive week. Empire manufacturing surged 18 pts to 25.5%; Philly Fed fell 17 pts to 20.9%.

bullets.title: AI credit stress front-and-center: HY spreads +59bps MoM to 324bp; CoreWeave CDS implies ~50% 5-yr default
bullets.body: High-yield OAS spreads widened 60bps over the month to 324bps, exceeding the 300bps threshold that historically triggers credit event risk. CoreWeave bonds trade at 78c on 15% yields; CDS implies ~50% 5-year default probability. IMF flagged AI investment as top financial stability risk, citing circular financing structures ($1.4tn promised revenue backed by $650bn debt, $300bn equity). JPM is hosting a dedicated AI financing credit call Friday covering hyperscaler capex durability and neocloud implications.

bullets.title: TSMC crushes estimates: raises 2026 revenue guide to +44%; 4Q guidance $53.3B vs. $50.1B consensus
bullets.body: TSMC reported 3Q revenue of $46.7B (beat vs. $45.4B consensus), guided 4Q to $53.3B vs. $50.1B street. Full-year 2026 revenue growth raised to +44% YoY vs. prior >40% guidance, driven by AI/HPC demand which is described as 'extremely robust with no signs of slowdown.' HPC revenue was 68% of mix (+22% q/q); 2nm contributed 8% of wafer revenue. Analyst estimates TSMC 2027 capex rising to $83-94B as N2 capacity doubles. Management confirmed advanced node prices rising 5-10% from 1Q27.

bullets.title: Anthropic revenue deceleration sparks AI infrastructure reassessment; ARR growth slowed from 147% to 45% YoY
bullets.body: Anthropic Q3 revenue hit $16.8B with the company profitable for the quarter, but YoY growth decelerated sharply from 147% to 45%. Treasury yields briefly rallied on the news as lower AI activity expectations imply lower growth and inflation. Multiple sources note the market wanted an S-1 filing and deeper disclosure; the AI capex ecosystem is not adapting plans overnight, but the ROIC-WACC spread is compressing precisely as cost of capital rises.

bullets.title: AI capex cycle intact but rate-sensitive now: consensus $500bn ARR may undershoot $7tn capex through 2030
bullets.body: 22V and Goldman both flag that the AI buildout, previously rate-insensitive when ROIC >> WACC and capex was self-funded, is now challenged as debt needs rise for $7tn in cumulative capex through 2030. Morgan Stanley forecasts $1.5tn hyperscaler capex in 2027 (+60% YoY); top-9 CSP capex raised to $1.5T+ for 2027 per MS TMT. If frontier lab revenue disappoints, more economic slowdown comes from AI rather than consumer — consumer cyclicals benefit on relative basis.

bullets.title: AI sell-off hitting semis and neoclouds hardest: CRWV -15%, DELL -11%, NBIS -10%, NVDA -3%
bullets.body: The CPI-driven risk rotation hit AI infrastructure names hardest in premarket and early trading: CRWV -15%, DELL -11%, NBIS -10%, NVDA -3%, TSM -3.5%, AVGO -3%, SNDK -5%, MU -4.5%, AMD -4.3%. Electronic Technology sector registered 0 new 52-week highs and 29 new lows. KOSPI crashed 7.6% on the day and is 39% from cycle peak, cited by Hedgeye as leading edge of AI bubble unwind.

bullets.title: Goldman flags under-hedged 'equities lower/yields lower' tail; proposes zero-cost USDJPY hedge
bullets.body: Goldman sees bull flattening and widening AI-related credit spreads as signaling growth and financing concerns beyond inflation. The firm proposes a zero-cost USDJPY digital spread (Buy 21Jan27 147.50 Binary Put / Sell 21Jan27 165.00 Binary Call at spot 157.95) to hedge the growth tail. Separately, Hedgeye notes the 10-year broke 5.10% trade level; trend threshold at 4.76%. Safe-haven flows are driving 10bp drops in 10-year yields despite hot macro data.

bullets.title: Hedgeye shifts to Quad 4 positioning: exits semis/Bitcoin, flips to consumer staples longs
bullets.body: Hedgeye's McCullough exited semiconductor exposure, reduced Bitcoin to 1% minimum after breaking $82k, and flipped consumer staples (XLP) bullish — adding Costco, Kroger, Philip Morris, Eli Lilly, Ralph Lauren to longs. He is short Russell 2000 on 11% drawdown, citing GDP and profit growth past cycle peaks, stronger dollar headwind, and small-cap financing constraints. S&P 500 risk range flagged at 7,652–7,828 with 7,731 as gamma line.

bullets.title: Data center power constraints now exceed supply constraints; 800VDC rollout slower than expected
bullets.body: OCP Day 3 takeaways show data center power constraints surpassing component supply constraints as the primary bottleneck. 800VDC rack shipments are expected only in small volumes in 2H27, primarily from Google, as NVIDIA Rubin Ultra racks may require lower power (~600kW or below) than anticipated. 35+ data center ballot measures on November 3 across 8 states (Ohio >50%) represent local zoning/moratorium risk to capex. Jefferies estimates ~65 IT GW under construction (~140% of installed capacity) with expected additions of 12.9 GW in 2026 and 18 GW in 2027.

bullets.title: Positioning setup may be near an inflection: Nasdaq/Russell gap at 99th percentile, historical bounce signal
bullets.body: JPM notes the Nasdaq vs. Russell positioning gap is now at the 99th percentile (+3.8z). Historically, SPX bounces 3.6% on average after strong selling combined with low positioning, with 7 of 10 instances being positive. T-Bond positioning is at the most net short in 12-month history (-3.7z). Jefferies notes mega-cap tech rotations historically last ~67 days with median -16.6% drawdown — still early if rotation is real.

bullets.title: Agentic AI now completing full travel bookings, bypassing OTAs entirely — commission pools at risk
bullets.body: Meta's Muse and Instinct are completing end-to-end travel bookings via browser automation and one-time cards, bypassing OTA platforms. Previous friction bottlenecks (payments, merchant of record) are now resolved in North America. OTA stocks are down 15-25% YTD following agentic AI launches; none of the 11 tracked OTA/hotel names has built systems allowing outside agents to complete bookings without handoff. Google rolled out hotel booking in AI Mode in late August.

bullets.title: AI neocloud financing model under stress: short-duration GPU assets financed with long-duration debt at 15% yields
bullets.body: Mizuho's Klein flags a structural mismatch in neocloud financing — using short-duration GPU assets financed with long-term debt, with debt yields hitting 15%. CoreWeave is spending at 4x operating cash flow, Oracle at 2x. DA Davidson upgraded CRWV to Buy with $110 PT citing de-risking, but UBS cut DOCN PT to $125 on financing headwinds (every 1% rise in cost of debt = ~$0.30 EPS hit to mid-2029 run-rate). Hyperscalers with stronger balance sheets are expected to benefit from neocloud stress.

bullets.title: September retail sales strong but inflation-driven; consumer electronics +8.8%, eCommerce +7.9%
bullets.body: UBS data shows unadjusted September retail sales rose 6.8% YoY (up from 4.9% in August), with CAGR since 2019 accelerating to 6.0%. Sporting goods +9.1%, consumer electronics +8.8%, eCommerce +7.9% YoY. However, Mizuho notes retail control group rose only 0.15% MoM vs. 0.3% consensus, with weakness in miscellaneous retailers (-3.02%) and sporting goods (-0.53%). Gasoline spend is climbing as a share of wallet (~12%), consistent with inflationary pressure on lower-income cohorts.

bullets.title: US midterms unlikely to shift AI or macro policy trajectory; hyperscaler capex at $1.5T for 2027
bullets.body: Morgan Stanley argues midterm results won't change the Trump administration's executive-led agenda on deregulation, tariffs, and trade. Federal AI legislation is likely to move slowly; state and local governments will be more influential on data center moratoriums and energy costs. Historical average S&P 500 return in the year following midterms with Republican president and split Congress is +23%.

bullets.title: TSMC strong, but semis investor base shifting: concentrating into optical/enterprise hardware, away from memory/semi caps
bullets.body: Mizuho's Klein notes the investor base is becoming more selective in semis, concentrating into optical, enterprise hardware, and CPUs while moving away from memory and semiconductor capital equipment. 1.6T AI networking shipments are beginning but 800G displacement rate is unclear; Roth is conducting channel checks on cannibalization. NVDA expanding Spectrum-X Ethernet adoption; optical vendors reporting 1.6T, near-packaged, and co-packaged optics activity.

bullets.title: Morgan Stanley bullish on mall revival: traffic positive, occupancy above pre-pandemic, Gen Z driving foot traffic
bullets.body: Morgan Stanley sees structural tailwinds for malls: 2026 traffic is positive reversing pre-Covid declines, occupancy is above pre-pandemic levels with tenants' sales per sq ft at new peaks, and e-commerce penetration in softlines has plateaued at ~40%. The mall-to-off-mall growth gap narrowed from ~500bps historically to ~200bps in 2025. Surviving malls have expanded restaurants/gyms/entertainment ~30% since 2019; Gen Z visits malls more than any other age cohort.

bullets.title: WFC beats but FICC misses; USB/PNC/BNY solid; AI credit risk cited as systemic financial stability concern
bullets.body: Bank earnings: WFC 3Q EPS $1.87 beat $1.84, with 4Q NII guidance ~$13B ahead of street ($12.8B) — NII/NIM inflecting higher for first time recently. PNC posted 13c EPS beat with loans +3% and deposits +4% q/q. BNY delivered 12c beat with fees +10% YoY. SCHW NII missed on NIM 3.04% vs. 3.08% consensus. Across the board, JPM financials desk flags AI financing as a systemic credit risk with widening spreads and deteriorating risk appetite.

bullets.title: China Q4 stimulus mostly ahead; GDP likely marginally above 4.5%; semiconductor export values +136% YoY but volume +1%
bullets.body: China September data provides a small Q4 positive with 800bn yuan fiscal stimulus still ahead, construction PMI rising to 50.3, and trade surplus hitting $133bn. However, export growth is price-driven not volume-driven — semiconductor values +136% YoY but volume +1% YoY. Households continue deleveraging; no additional stimulus expected before year-end. Full-year GDP expected marginally above 4.5%.
